record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: Borderline regularity for hearing the degree
record.original_question: Suppose f,g:S^1→S^1 have equal Fourier coefficient moduli |an(f)|=|an(g)| for every n∈Z. The equality deg f=deg g is known when f,g ∈ W^{1/3,3}(S^1;S^1), and also for Hölder maps of exponent α>1/3. Does the same conclusion hold when f,g ∈ W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1) with p>3, or when f,g are Hölder with exponent α≤1/3? What happens under the asymmetric stronger assumptions f ∈ W^{1/p,p}, 2<p≤3, g ∈ W^{1/q,q}, q>3, or f ∈ C^{0,α}, α>1/3, g ∈ C^{0,β}, β≤1/3?

evidence.quote: Theorem 5.5 ([Br7, Corollary 2], [BM, Corollary 12.3], [Ka]). Assume that f, g ∈ W1/3,3(S1; S1) satisfy |an(f)| = |an(g)| ∀n ∈ Z, then deg f = deg g. In particular the conclusion holds if f, g ∈ C0,α(S1; S1) with α > 1/3.

Open Problem 5.5. What happens to Theorem 5.5 when f, g ∈ W1/p,p(S1; S1) with p > 3 (resp. f, g ∈ C0,α(S1: S1) with α ≤ 1/3)? The problem is open even under the stronger assumption that f ∈ W1/p,p with 2 < p ≤ 3 and g ∈ W1/q,q with q > 3 (resp. f ∈ C0,α with α > 1/3 and g ∈ C0,β with β ≤ 1/3).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle. For a measurable map $h:S^1\to S^1\subset\mathbb{C}$, write its Fourier coefficients as
$$a_n(h)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{S^1} h(\theta)\,e^{-in\theta}\,d\theta,\qquad n\in\mathbb{Z}.$$
For sufficiently regular maps $h:S^1\to S^1$ (e.g., continuous), let $\deg h\in\mathbb{Z}$ denote the topological (winding) degree. For $1\le p<\infty$ and $s\in(0,1)$, the fractional Sobolev space $W^{s,p}(S^1;S^1)$ consists of measurable maps $h:S^1\to S^1$ with
$$\iint_{S^1\times S^1}\frac{|h(x)-h(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{1+sp}}\,dx\,dy<\infty,$$
and $C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ denotes Hölder-continuous maps of exponent $\alpha\in(0,1]$.

It is known that if $f,g\in W^{1/3,3}(S^1;S^1)$ satisfy $|a_n(f)|=|a_n(g)|$ for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, then $\deg f=\deg g$; in particular this conclusion holds when $f,g\in C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ with $\alpha>1/3$.

Questions:
(a) Does the conclusion $\deg f=\deg g$ remain true if instead $f,g\in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$ for some $p>3$?
(b) Does it remain true if $f,g\in C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ with $\alpha\le 1/3$?
(c) Is it true under the asymmetric hypotheses $f\in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$ with $2<p\le 3$ and $g\in W^{1/q,q}(S^1;S^1)$ with $q>3$?
(d) Is it true under the asymmetric hypotheses $f\in C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ with $\alpha>1/3$ and $g\in C^{0,\beta}(S^1;S^1)$ with $\beta\le 1/3$?
